data.name: Alaska
data.summary: Alaska's Rural Health Transformation Program is in active statewide implementation, coordinated by the Department of Health with oversight from an Advisory Council and broad stakeholder engagement. The program launched in early 2026, following regional planning meetings and a robust Letter of Interest process, with current efforts guided by six interconnected initiatives focused on maternal and child health, workforce development, access to care, healthy communities, fiscal sustainability, and technology modernization. Project awards are being announced on a rolling basis, with Year 1 performance periods now underway and weekly funding updates ongoing. Current structured plan tracks 13 key initiatives and 19 strategic goals.

data.name: Alabama
data.summary: The Alabama Rural Health Transformation Program (ARHTP), led by ADECA, is actively implementing 11 statewide initiatives focused on enhancing access, provider sustainability, workforce development, care delivery, and technology integration in rural communities. Guided by an executive order-established Advisory Group, ARHTP utilizes a phased Notice of Funding Opportunity approach targeting areas such as EHR/IT, EMS trauma and stroke, maternal health, cancer digital regionalization, simulation training, and workforce initiatives. The program follows the CMS Rural Health Transformation framework, emphasizing multi-year planning, measurable progress, and structured annual review for sustained rural health system improvement. The current implementation plan tracks 11 major initiatives aligned with strategic goals, with Year 1 funding cycles completed and Year 2 scheduled to begin in October 2026. Current structured plan tracks 12 key initiatives and 7 strategic goals.

data.name: Arkansas
data.summary: Arkansas’s Rural Health Transformation Program is currently in active implementation, with applications open for initiative funding through HEART, RISE, PACT, and THRIVE. The program focuses on improving access, population health, telehealth integration, workforce development, and emergency services modernization across high-need rural regions, guided by ongoing stakeholder input. Behavioral health transition services and community partnership networks remain priority focus areas. Current structured plan tracks 10 key initiatives and 8 strategic goals.

data.name: Arizona
data.summary: The Arizona Rural Health Transformation Program (RHTP), administered by AHCCCS, is actively implemented and operating, with major grant initiatives continuing through at least 2026. RHTP maintains its focus on workforce development, access to care, health system strengthening, and collaborative approaches for rural and Tribal communities. Applicants must attest to fiscal stewardship and the non-supplanting of funds, and the program has structured oversight with a current plan tracking multiple key initiatives and strategic goals within a defined governance framework. Current structured plan tracks 10 key initiatives and 7 strategic goals.

data.name: California
data.summary: The California Rural Health Transformation (CalRHT) Program is in early implementation, administered by the Department of Health Care Access and Information with CMS oversight. The program aims to build a connected and resilient rural health system, with major focus areas including workforce development, technology and EHR modernization, regional rural collaboratives, and sustained community engagement. Current efforts emphasize launching grants for workforce recruitment and retention, telehealth expansion, financial stability, and infrastructure upgrades, all guided by a structured plan and regular stakeholder input through the Rural Health Policy Council. The structured plan continues to track key initiatives and strategic goals informed by ongoing council meetings and partner engagement. Current structured plan tracks 10 key initiatives and 10 strategic goals.

data.name: Colorado
data.summary: The Colorado Rural Health Transformation Program (RHTP) is a federally funded initiative administered by the Department of Health Care Policy and Financing (HCPF), currently in the application and contracting phase for the 2026–2027 grant cycle, with technical assistance from the Colorado Rural Health Center. The program supports rural and frontier providers through a structured eligibility and application process, oversight by an Advisory Committee, and grants for workforce, provider stability, health IT, EMS, maternal/perinatal health, minor renovations (now up to 20% of budgets), and innovative care models. Focus areas include measurable outcomes, regional collaboration, completion of projects by September 30, 2027, and adherence to updated eligibility and allowable use guidance. Current cycle activities feature active stakeholder engagement, updated budget guidance, events supporting applicants, and a rigorous review process ahead of award announcements anticipated by September 2026. Current structured plan tracks 19 key initiatives and 13 strategic goals.

data.name: Connecticut
data.summary: Connecticut's Rural Health Transformation Program (RHTP) is currently in the implementation phase, led by the Department of Social Services and developed through sustained stakeholder engagement and broad public input. The program focuses on four core areas—population health outcomes, workforce development, data and technology modernization, and care transformation and stability—organizing projects that include mobile clinics, workforce pipelines, community health navigators, and integration with Connecticut's health information exchange. Structured plans track progress toward key initiatives and strategic goals, with ongoing collaborations and regular input from a Rural Health Advisory Council as implementation progresses. Current structured plan tracks 10 key initiatives and 10 strategic goals.

data.name: Delaware
data.summary: Delaware’s Rural Health Transformation Program is actively implementing a comprehensive strategy, with initial RFPs released to establish the state's first four-year medical school, expand school-based health centers in Sussex County, build Food Is Medicine infrastructure, and deploy rural health hubs including mobile health unit networks. The program prioritizes rural care disparities through projects focused on access, prevention, nutrition-integrated care, workforce development, telehealth, and health information exchange, leveraging competitive funding and partnerships for sustainability and measurable outcomes. The structured plan tracks key initiatives and strategic goals, emphasizing innovative access models and improved health equity. Current structured plan tracks 15 key initiatives and 9 strategic goals.

data.name: Florida
data.summary: Florida's Rural Health Transformation Program, administered by the Agency for Health Care Administration, is currently implementing competitive Requests for Applications through MyFloridaMarketPlace for fiscal year 2026, targeting rural provider organizations and underserved communities. The program prioritizes statewide access, rural hospital capacity, workforce expansion, innovative care delivery, Medicaid value-based purchasing, and strategic investments in specialty, acute, and behavioral health services, care-at-home models, and infrastructure for value-based payment readiness. Current structured plan tracks 18 key initiatives and 10 strategic goals.

data.name: Georgia
data.summary: Georgia's Rural Health Transformation Program, under the GREAT Health initiative, is in active multi-year implementation across 126 HRSA-designated rural counties, operationalizing a federally supported value-based care transformation model. The current focus includes technology-driven workforce retention strategies such as surgical robotics, expanded newborn screening, telehealth enhancements, behavioral health interventions, cybersecurity, and workforce recruitment via nursing education, scholarships, EMS, and medical training partnerships. Technology-enabled workforce stabilization and public health system expansion remain central priorities. Current structured plan tracks 15 key initiatives and 11 strategic goals.

data.name: Hawaii
data.summary: The Hawaii Rural Health Transformation Program (RHTP) is currently in active planning and early implementation, following a recent annual award supporting major initiatives to strengthen rural health systems. The program focuses on advancing value-based payment reform, aligning with the AHEAD model through IT upgrades, hospital and provider supports, and quality-focused initiatives managed by SHPDA, DOH, and Med-QUEST. Hospital-specific analysis and system alignments are underway, with significant payment transformation scheduled to begin in 2028.

data.name: Iowa
data.summary: The Iowa Rural Health Transformation Program leverages federal funding and interactive dashboards to guide implementation and assess outcomes across rural communities. Currently in pilot and early award phases, the program emphasizes hub-and-spoke models, provider partnerships, expanded workforce recruitment through new and expanded rural residencies, health information exchange enhancements, EMS-led mobile integrated health, and the development of health hubs focused on cancer and service co-location. Efforts are organized under five principal initiatives—Hometown Connections, Combat Cancer, Communities of Care, Health Information Exchange, and EMS Community Care Mobile—with progress monitored via structured initiatives and strategic goals. Current structured plan tracks 10 key initiatives and 10 strategic goals.

data.name: Idaho
data.summary: Idaho's Rural Health Transformation Program is in its initial implementation phase under the Department of Health and Welfare, guided by broad stakeholder and task force input, including legislators and tribal representatives. Building on an organized plan, the program advances workforce development, innovative care models, technology and cybersecurity modernization, evidence-based interventions, and facility upgrades, with contracts and subgrants progressing through mid to late 2026 and full obligation of Year 1 funds by October 2026. Current initiatives prioritize rural provider capacity, maternal and behavioral health, infrastructure improvements, and now include targeted cognitive care networks and chronic disease prevention efforts, structured around five key focus areas and an organized tracking of strategic goals and initiatives. Recent competitive solicitations reflect targeted efforts in health workforce, perinatal collaborations, facility modernization, health IT security, cognitive care, and chronic disease prevention. Current structured plan tracks 21 key initiatives and 12 strategic goals.

data.name: Illinois
data.summary: Illinois is currently implementing the Rural Health Transformation Program following federal award approval, focusing on expanding equitable access and reducing barriers to healthcare in rural regions. Major areas include hospital transformation, workforce development, technology-enabled care, and advancing maternal and chronic disease priorities, with multi-year initiatives and stakeholder engagement ongoing. Illinois Department of Healthcare and Family Services is actively establishing governance structures, issuing NOFOs, and preparing first-year fund distribution. Efforts involve regional partnerships and telehealth expansion to improve health outcomes for rural residents, with progress tracked by structured plans and strategic goals. Current structured plan tracks 17 key initiatives and 12 strategic goals.

data.name: Indiana
data.summary: Indiana’s Rural Health Transformation Program (RHTP) is currently active, pursuing a five-year plan with statewide and regional initiatives under the GROW program. Led by the Indiana Department of Health and Family and Social Services Administration, the program’s focus areas include rural care coordination, specialty and telehealth access, digital infrastructure modernization, workforce development, and improvements in maternal, pediatric, and emergency care. Ongoing program implementation is demonstrated by interconnected initiatives, structured tracking, regional grants, and strategic evaluation activities. Current plans define a dozen key initiatives and strategic goals addressing care coordination, infrastructure improvement, workforce strengthening, and expanded access to rural health services. Current structured plan tracks 25 key initiatives and 18 strategic goals.

data.name: Kansas
data.summary: The Kansas Rural Health Transformation Program, administered by KDHE with partners such as the Kansas Rural Health Innovation Alliance and Healthworks, is actively implementing structured initiatives to enhance rural health outcomes through innovative care models, technology adoption, workforce pipeline development, and pilot programs in areas like dementia care and chronic disease management. Current focus areas include Emerging Technology grants for rural providers, centralized credentialing, revenue technical support, Community Health Worker and Food is Medicine projects, workforce programs, and the Interfacility Transport Project. The program maintains a structured plan with multiple strategic initiatives and ongoing progress tracking to expand access and quality for rural residents. Multiple funding opportunities are currently open across key focus areas for rural providers and facilities. Current structured plan tracks 13 key initiatives and 12 strategic goals.

data.name: Kentucky
data.summary: The Kentucky Rural Health Transformation Program is actively implementing initiatives in community health worker training, EMS transformation, behavioral health crisis response, rural dental access, chronic care, maternal health, and regional health hub development. Multiple funding opportunities and structured applications are open for health departments, EMS agencies, behavioral health organizations, and educational institutions, with major focus on technology-enabled care and multisector collaboration. The current plan emphasizes coordinated statewide efforts and tracks progress across initiatives through 2026. Current structured plan tracks 9 key initiatives and 5 strategic goals.

data.name: Louisiana
data.summary: The Louisiana Rural Health Transformation Program, led by the Louisiana Department of Health, is progressing through its first budget year with active implementation of structured initiatives in workforce development, value-based care, telehealth, infrastructure, EMS, interoperability, and rural health innovation. The program coordinates healthcare providers, community organizations, technology partners, educational institutions, and state agencies to improve rural health outcomes, reduce disparities, and foster sustainable care delivery. Multiple competitive funding opportunities and program applications remain open through August 2026, supporting provider networks, regional care coordination, and innovation. Current structured plan tracks 10 key initiatives and 10 strategic goals.

data.name: Massachusetts
data.summary: Massachusetts was awarded $162 million in December 2025 to support rural healthcare transformation. The program's vision is a Commonwealth where rural communities thrive, focusing on access, well-being, and resilient systems. The HCWC State Office of Rural Health leads these efforts with targeted initiatives and partnerships. Current structured plan tracks 7 key initiatives and 3 strategic goals.

data.name: Maryland
data.summary: Maryland's Rural Health Transformation Program, administered by the State Office of Rural Health, is in active implementation following its federal award in December 2025, with major initiatives targeting state-designated rural areas. Centered on three pillars—workforce transformation, sustainable access and innovative care, and healthy food initiatives—the program currently emphasizes expanding primary and behavioral health care, provider workforce development and training, telehealth infrastructure deployment, and food infrastructure improvements. Competitive procurements and active projects support workforce pathways, care integration, and rural data analysis. The plan maintains focused efforts to address rural healthcare disparities and provider shortages through collaborative state and partner management, tracking multiple key initiatives and strategic goals. Current structured plan tracks 10 key initiatives and 6 strategic goals.

data.name: Maine
data.summary: Maine's Rural Health Transformation Program is a federally funded, multi-year initiative in active implementation, guided by five strategic initiatives: population health, workforce, technology and innovation, access, and sustainability. The current focus includes electronic medical record modernization, workforce development, hospital financial efficiency, and expanding digital health infrastructure, with Year 1 funding opportunities underway for provider and community organizations. The structured plan tracks progress against strategic goals and timelines and is supported by ongoing advisory and provider engagement activities. Current structured plan tracks 10 key initiatives and 6 strategic goals.

data.name: Michigan
data.summary: Michigan’s Rural Health Transformation Program is in its initial implementation phase for FY 2026–2030 following CMS approval and federal award, led by the Michigan Department of Health and Human Services. The program is advancing planning, competitive grant solicitations, and building regional partnerships, supported by an advisory council of rural health stakeholders. Current priorities include workforce capacity, health information technology and telehealth, care coordination, behavioral and chronic disease health, transportation access, and transparent distribution of funding. Current structured plan tracks 7 key initiatives and 10 strategic goals.

data.name: Minnesota
data.summary: The Minnesota Rural Health Transformation Program, administered by the Department of Health's Office of Rural Health and Primary Care, began implementation in December 2025 with milestones extending through October 2030. The program supports workforce retention and expansion—including clinical fellowships, loan repayment, and child/adolescent mental health—technology adoption, provider collaboration, and targeted improvements in chronic disease, maternal, and behavioral health outcomes for rural and Tribal communities. It actively engages Tribal partners and rural care sites through structured RFPs for hospitals, clinics, health centers, and clinicians, and oversees key initiatives aligned with strategic goals. The current structured plan tracks ongoing implementation across major focus areas including telehealth access, technical assistance, and Project ECHO. Current structured plan tracks 15 key initiatives and 13 strategic goals.

data.name: Missouri
data.summary: Missouri's Rural Health Transformation Program (RHTP), administered by the MO HealthNet Division and Department of Social Services, remains in active implementation and continues its focus on the ToRCH Care model, which establishes Community Hubs to coordinate clinical and non-clinical services across rural regions. Major current priorities include nurse home visiting, expansion of maternal, behavioral health, diagnostic/outpatient, and chronic disease management services, as well as modernization of rural hospital and health center infrastructure. Active initiatives further advance Mobile Integrated Healthcare–Community Paramedicine system expansion, facility upgrades, and strengthening regional partnerships led by 27 Hub Anchor organizations. The program is guided by a structured plan with tracked initiatives and strategic goals, as confirmed in recent funding and implementation documents. Current structured plan tracks 21 key initiatives and 10 strategic goals.

data.name: Mississippi
data.summary: The Mississippi Rural Health Transformation Program is presently in its initial implementation stage, coordinated by the Governor's Office and state agencies, and is rolling out grant initiatives to support workforce expansion, psychiatric emergency services (EmPATH Units), and EMS capacity assessment. Current efforts remain focused on workforce recruitment and retention, psychiatric crisis care expansion, EMS regional organization, telehealth expansion, technology upgrades, and provider infrastructure improvements. Current structured plan tracks 13 key initiatives and 12 strategic goals.

data.name: Montana
data.summary: Montana is actively implementing the Rural Health Transformation Program, guided by a structured transformation plan that emphasizes workforce development, sustainable access, innovative care models, community health and prevention, and technology innovation. Led by DPHHS with oversight by Stakeholder Advisory and Center of Excellence councils, the program broadly engages tribal nations, providers, nonprofits, educational institutions, and agencies. Current activities include ongoing grants, contracts, and initiative tracking across major focus areas, with the Center of Excellence supporting rural health system sustainability. Current structured plan tracks 14 key initiatives and 13 strategic goals.

data.name: North Carolina
data.summary: North Carolina's Rural Health Transformation Program is advancing toward implementation with initial activities beginning in mid-2026, establishing six regional NC ROOTS Hubs led by designated organizations to coordinate rural health transformation initiatives. Major focus areas include launching regionally governed hubs to integrate medical, behavioral, and social health services; expanding chronic disease and maternal health care; workforce development; provider support for value-based care; and digital health innovation. Program activities will operate across 85 rural counties, overseen by a statewide steering committee prioritizing transparency and broad stakeholder engagement, and organized around six strategies over five years. Current structured plan tracks 17 key initiatives and 15 strategic goals.

data.name: North Dakota
data.summary: The North Dakota Rural Health Transformation Program is actively launching phased, competitive funding rounds targeting workforce stabilization, preventive care, behavioral health, and health technology modernization in rural and tribal communities. Current focus areas include workforce training and retention, safety net service delivery, telehealth and remote monitoring, and data and infrastructure upgrades designed to support measurable, sustainable improvements in health care access and outcomes. Administered by North Dakota Health and Human Services, the program partners with communities and Critical Access Hospitals, emphasizing evidence-based initiatives and operational sustainability. Multiple structured grant opportunities remain open and are tracked across key strategic pillars, with progress monitored against established goals and initiatives. Current structured plan tracks 26 key initiatives and 9 strategic goals.

data.name: Nebraska
data.summary: The Nebraska Rural Health Transformation Program is in its initial implementation stage, launching statewide initiatives beginning in Spring 2026, with rolling funding opportunities for rural providers each year. Major focus areas include food as medicine, emergency and behavioral health, workforce acceleration, eHealth, and facility modernization, with active oversight by the Nebraska Department of Health and Human Services and structured input from newly established Health Care Advisory Regions. The program emphasizes technology-enabled solutions, regional care coordination, and addresses critical rural workforce and health access gaps. Current structured plan tracks 14 key initiatives and 15 strategic goals.

data.name: New Hampshire
data.summary: The New Hampshire Rural Health Transformation Program, administered by GO-NORTH and the Foundation for Healthy Communities and funded by CMS for 2026–2030, is currently in the implementation phase, with contracts awarded and multiple competitive funding opportunities underway. Major focus areas include modernization of rural healthcare access and quality, facility and workforce improvements, expanded oral health, EMS, and primary care initiatives, enhancements to telehealth and IT infrastructure, and sustainability through innovative care models. Hub organizations and cross-sector collaboration remain central to program delivery, with progress tracked through a structured plan comprising strategic initiatives and goals. Current structured plan tracks 21 key initiatives and 12 strategic goals.

data.name: New Jersey
data.summary: The New Jersey Rural Health Transformation Program (RHTP) is currently advancing a structured set of initiatives focused on technology deployment, prevention, workforce training, and capacity development for rural hospitals, community health workers, doula integration, and EMS/dispatch enhancements. The program is actively connecting rural providers and organizations with approved vendors via an up-to-date resource directory, issuing new grant opportunities, and accelerating implementation with strategic partnerships. Current structured plan tracks 15 key initiatives and 15 strategic goals.

data.name: New Mexico
data.summary: Major focus areas include workforce development, system sustainability, community-based innovation, and improved access to care—including specialty, maternal, behavioral health, and chronic disease services—for rural, frontier, and tribal populations. The program emphasizes enhancing infrastructure, advancing health equity, supporting local solutions, and integrating health data through strategic investments. Current implementation (2026–2030) is guided by a structured plan with annual performance-based funding, and major procurement opportunities are actively underway for initiatives such as the Administrative Services Organization, Center for Rural Health Sustainability & Innovation, Healthy Horizons, Rooted in New Mexico, Rural Health Innovation Fund, and the Rural Health Data Hub, all supporting statewide transformation goals. Current structured plan tracks 6 key initiatives and 6 strategic goals.

data.name: Nevada
data.summary: The RHTP is administered by the Nevada Health Authority (NVHA) with support from CMS through a federal cooperative agreement. Multiple funding opportunities are available in 2026, targeting areas like rural health innovation, workforce recruitment, tribal health systems, and provider infrastructure. Applicants are advised to review RFA documents for eligibility and guidance. Current structured plan tracks 12 key initiatives and 15 strategic goals.

data.name: New York
data.summary: New York's Rural Health Transformation Program is actively implementing a multi-initiative plan following its November 2025 CMS application and first-year federal award. The program focuses on Rural Community Health Integration, partnership building, technology-enhanced and AI-supported primary care, expanding telehealth and cybersecurity for rural providers, and rural workforce development. The state is currently finalizing contracts, launching procurements, and releasing new funding guidance, with rural planning and implementation applications due by July 14, 2026, and contracts scheduled from September 1, 2026 through June 30, 2027. Program activities are structured around four main initiatives—health network integration, technology-enhanced care, workforce development, and cybersecurity—supporting healthcare delivery and sustainability for rural communities. Current structured plan tracks 5 key initiatives and 7 strategic goals.

data.name: Ohio
data.summary: The Ohio Rural Health Transformation Program is actively implementing recurring, competitive solicitations targeting workforce upskilling, pharmacy transformation, chronic disease prevention, technical assistance, and the expansion of school-based and clinically integrated rural health networks. Structured bidders conferences and coordinated timelines support applicant participation, with the Ohio Department of Health overseeing communications and program management. Major initiatives focus on building rural workforce pipelines, community health worker training, and strengthening rural health delivery systems, guided by a structured plan tracking key initiatives and strategic goals. Current implementation includes the launch of the first awarded project to Ohio University for rural workforce development, multi-partner collaborations, and ongoing solicitations across several initiative tracks. Current structured plan tracks 13 key initiatives and 6 strategic goals.

data.name: Oklahoma
data.summary: The Oklahoma Rural Health Transformation Program (RHTP) is actively implementing a federally supported, multi-year initiative to expand rural health access, quality, and sustainability statewide. RHTP prioritizes improving care closer to home through telehealth, transportation reimbursement, local infrastructure investments, workforce development, advanced technology, EMS centralization with platforms like Pulsara, behavioral health integration, and innovative care models, guided by extensive statewide engagement and competitive grant opportunities. The current structured plan tracks key initiatives and strategic goals, with phased implementation, regional events, and ongoing statewide launches informing priorities and targeted funding. Current structured plan tracks 16 key initiatives and 10 strategic goals.

data.name: Oregon
data.summary: Oregon's Rural Health Transformation Program is actively implementing for 2026, administering Catalyst and Immediate Impact Awards to over 130 rural health projects statewide. The Oregon Health Authority, in partnership with CMS, leads a structured plan focused on five major initiatives: regional partnerships, healthy communities, workforce capacity, technology and data modernization, and a Tribal Initiative, with priority areas in maternal/child and behavioral health. Regional convenings and collaboratives continue to support technical assistance, coordination, and preparation for future funding. The program currently supports the largest single round of RHTP grantmaking in the state’s history and tracks key initiatives and strategic goals. Current structured plan tracks 12 key initiatives and 17 strategic goals.

data.name: Pennsylvania
data.summary: The Pennsylvania Rural Health Transformation Program is currently active, providing direct funding to rural healthcare providers and facilities for supplies, equipment, and technology modernization. Major focus areas include certified EHR and Health Information Organizations onboarding, workforce development, behavioral health, EMS, maternal health, aging access, and rural clinic connectivity, anchored by targeted initiatives including the Rapid Response Stabilization and EHR & HIO modernization rounds. Funding is administered through coordinated state mechanisms with defined eligibility and regional limits, focusing on six main RHTP initiatives; strategic goals and progress are tracked under an established framework. Current implementation includes open application periods and per-location award caps for 2026 funding rounds. Current structured plan tracks 11 key initiatives and 10 strategic goals.

data.name: Rhode Island
data.summary: Rhode Island is implementing the Rural Health Transformation Program across 18 rural towns and the Narragansett Indian Tribe, coordinated by EOHHS and RIDOH with input from the Rural Stakeholder Advisory Council. The program focuses on expanding access to care (including FQHCs and hospital-at-home), workforce development, advancing value-based care, behavioral health, digital infrastructure modernization, and health equity. Current efforts prioritize robust stakeholder engagement, launching Rural Community Health Networks, and monitoring progress toward strategic goals, with a structured plan currently tracking key initiatives and goals. Multiple procurement opportunities and active community-driven initiatives mark the present implementation phase. Current structured plan tracks 20 key initiatives and 8 strategic goals.

data.name: South Carolina
data.summary: The South Carolina Rural Health Transformation Program is currently offering one-time infrastructure and capacity-building grants through four targeted initiatives: Connections to Care, Wellness Within Reach, Leveling Up, and Shoring Up to Sustainability. The program focuses on expanding digital infrastructure, scaling successful pilot programs, deploying mobile health units, and strengthening healthcare systems in rural communities, with applications due June 1, 2026. Implementation is underway, with subrecipient agreements being distributed and oversight responsibilities established, aligned to CMS strategic goals and federal regulations. Current structured plan tracks 10 key initiatives and 9 strategic goals.

data.name: South Dakota
data.summary: The South Dakota Rural Health Transformation Program is actively implementing its fiscal year 2026 plan, emphasizing digital health modernization, community health worker and workforce development (including maternal health training), EMS advancement, and sustainable systems transformation. The Department of Health administers structured grant programs supporting behavioral health, chronic disease management, infrastructure, and Medicaid Primary Accountable Care Transformation through formal RFP processes and provider technical assistance. Current structured plan tracks 22 key initiatives and 11 strategic goals.

data.name: Tennessee
data.summary: The Tennessee Rural Health Transformation Program is actively implemented through a phased plan focused on reversing rural hospital decline, expanding care access, and modernizing healthcare delivery and technology. Recent efforts include multiple competitive grant opportunities and procurement cycles, notably through the Rural Healthcare Access Modernization Program (RAMP), emphasizing improvements in behavioral health, chronic disease prevention, maternal and child health, innovation, workforce stability, and healthcare resiliency. Ongoing implementation features newly released and scheduled grant categories, RFPs, and prioritized support to rural providers and organizations. Current structured plan tracks 19 key initiatives and 13 strategic goals.

data.name: Texas
data.summary: The Texas Rural Health Transformation Program (RHTP), administered by HHSC as Rural Texas Strong, supports rural hospitals and providers with a current focus on strengthening rural healthcare capacity through workforce development, innovative service delivery, telehealth, infrastructure upgrades, and hospital viability. The program is actively implementing targeted initiatives, grant rounds, and solicitations for provider training, partnerships, behavioral health, and addressing unmet needs in rural communities. Public forums, structured plans, and collaborations guide ongoing efforts, with current implementation centered on six major initiatives tracked within the Rural Texas Strong plan. Current structured plan tracks 15 key initiatives and 12 strategic goals.

data.name: Federal
data.summary: The Federal Rural Health Transformation Program (RHTP), authorized by federal law, is a $50 billion initiative supporting rural health system transformation across all 50 states from FY2026 to FY2030. The program is in its application and early implementation phase, focusing on rural hospital stabilization, workforce recruitment and retention—including service commitments—technology advancement, evidence-based health interventions, and expanding access to care through innovative models. States are required to submit comprehensive transformation plans, demonstrate progress on approved initiatives, and comply with annual reporting requirements. Current program structure tracks major initiatives and strategic goals, with strict guidelines for fund use and modification. Current structured plan tracks 14 key initiatives and 12 strategic goals.

data.name: Utah
data.summary: Utah's Rural Health Transformation Program is in early implementation, led by the Utah Department of Health and Human Services with major CMS federal support and funding anticipated through 2030. Its structured plan includes phased deliverables, multisectoral partnerships, and an emphasis on sustainable infrastructure and technology enhancement through specific initiatives like SHIFT and LINCS. Current structured plan tracks 10 key initiatives and 5 strategic goals.

data.name: Virginia
data.summary: Virginia’s Rural Health Transformation Program is actively implementing a multi-year statewide initiative focused on workforce development, technology modernization—including remote patient monitoring and provider interoperability—care delivery innovation, and expanded care models. The program currently administers competitive funding opportunities for rural providers, with structured program planning, stakeholder engagement, and technical assistance for applicants. Progress is tracked through defined strategic goals and sub-initiatives, with current open RFAs supporting digital productivity tools, EHR modernization, and workforce recruitment and training to improve rural health access and care innovation. Key activities are coordinated by the VHHA Foundation with multiple opportunities available for rural health organizations in 2026. Current structured plan tracks 16 key initiatives and 7 strategic goals.

data.name: Vermont
data.summary: Vermont's Rural Health Transformation Program, administered by the Vermont Agency of Human Services and funded by CMS, completed Year 1 grantmaking and contracting and is now in early implementation, with planning for Year 2 underway. The program is anchored by five main strategic initiatives—regionalization of care, shared clinical services, strengthening primary care, workforce development, and price transparency—and supports 36 activities, including workforce training, expanded dialysis and ventilator services, and telehealth. Progress is tracked against strategic goals through a structured, multi-year approach that coordinates federal and state resources to strengthen provider capacity and transform the rural health system. Current planning emphasizes improved access, workforce expansion, system interoperability, and innovative care models for rural and high-need populations. Current structured plan tracks 10 key initiatives and 7 strategic goals.

data.name: Washington
data.summary: Washington is actively implementing the Rural Health Transformation Program to advance rural hospital innovation, workforce development, care access, technology adoption, and community health. Efforts focus on system transformation with priorities shaped by stakeholder and tribal engagement, behavioral health, provider technology, and workforce support for opioid and specialty services. The first performance period begins December 2025, under a long-term strategy rather than short-term grantmaking. The program is administered by HCA and partners, with current efforts structured around multiple initiatives and strategic goals. Current structured plan tracks 15 key initiatives and 13 strategic goals.

data.name: Wisconsin
data.summary: The Wisconsin Rural Health Transformation Program is implementing a statewide portfolio of workforce, technology, and partnership initiatives, funded by a multi-year CMS grant and led by the Department of Health Services with advisory council input. Key focus areas include strengthening the rural healthcare workforce, advancing digital infrastructure, and improving care coordination through collaboration with educational, public health, and tribal organizations. Current structured efforts track multiple initiatives such as workforce development, technology upgrades, coordinated care models, youth mental health interventions, and Community Health Worker training. Several targeted grant opportunities are active or have recently closed, reflecting ongoing program implementation and oversight. Current structured plan tracks 9 key initiatives and 9 strategic goals.

data.name: West Virginia
data.summary: West Virginia's Rural Health Transformation Program (RHTP) is actively implementing competitive funding opportunities to expand EMS-driven community paramedicine and mobile-integrated health care models, supported by the Connected Care Grid pillar to improve access and integration in rural regions. The program is currently launching the Smart Care Catalyst initiative to design, implement, and scale PACE-aligned care models for older adults with complex needs, while maintaining multi-payer payment standards and a milestone-based framework to ensure program sustainability. Ongoing outreach, advisory panel engagement, and technical assistance are provided for applicants, with emphasis on EMS-led care, aging in place, enhanced care coordination, transportation access, workforce support, and statewide data integration. Current structured plan tracks 20 key initiatives and 18 strategic goals.
